about_item: EMERGENCY DOG CARRYING SLING: The Airlift is designed for hiking, skiing, and other outdoor activities, allowing you to safely carry your injured or sick dog using this dog lift from the trail to safety, even in rugged terrain.

LIGHTWEIGHT AND PACKABLE: Weighing just 13 oz, this incredibly lightweight rescue sling for dogs fits into a small stuff sack, making it an essential addition to store in your backpack to ensure you're always prepared for emergencies.

8-POINT SUPPORT FOR SAFE TRANSPORT: This dog carry sling features an 8-point support system that cradles your dog, evenly distributing weight from head to tail for a comfortable and secure carry, ideal for paralyzed dogs during rescue situations.
FITS MEDIUM-SIZED DOGS (20-45 LBS): The Fido Pro Airlift in Red (Size M) is a medium dog sling designed for dogs weighing 20-45 lbs, with a body length of 9-14 inches.

TRUSTED BY VETERINARIANS AND SEARCH & RESCUE: Rigorously tested in the toughest conditions, the Airlift emergency dog sling is trusted by veterinarians and Search & Rescue professionals, ensuring its reliability when you need it most.

authors_reviews.title: Peace of Mind For Our Adventures
authors_reviews.text: We do a lot of hiking with our pup and I started to worry about how we might get him to safety should he get injured. While he's only 19-20lbs., that's a good bit to carry over a long distance for two middle-aged people. After asking around in hiking groups what others were using, this was recommended over and over. We've put him in it and carried him around the house and it works really well. He's as comfortable as can be and the weight distribution works for either me or my husband so we now feel confident we can get him back to any trailhead we might be on. It folds up small and weighs very little but seems very durable. I hope we never have to use it but the peace of mind I have on trail now is worth the money!
authors_reviews.author: Bee A.

authors_reviews.title: Adventure dog essential
authors_reviews.text: I cannot say enough good things about this product and company. As an avid hiker in the mountains of CO, I adopted my cattle dog, Otis, hoping he would become a fulltime adventure companion. After 3 years together, he loves nothing more than a hiking trail! I bought one of these direct from fido pro along with the first hiking gear I bought for Otis. The one I bought here was a gift for my girlfriend and her pup. We've tested the sling but, fortunately, we haven't needed it yet for real. This is like an airbag, or the flotation vests on a plane. You hope you never need it, but having it ready is essential. There are certainly other cheaper and more cushioned options for lifting your dog, but none of them are designed to fit into a small backpack like this one is. The name of the game here is functional, and that comes at the expense of comfortable. There is no better choice for hiking safety for your dog, and every hiking dog should have one!
authors_reviews.author: ooocarl06

authors_reviews.title: Good but heavy
authors_reviews.text: I haven’t had to use it yet, but carrying it with me when hiking and backpacking. I do wish it was a little lighter, it’s hard to justify the weight for a “maybe” when backpacking. It seems usable for an emergency.
authors_reviews.author: Amanda E.

authors_reviews.title: Works Perfectly
authors_reviews.text: My daughter hikes with our older dog Storm and was worried about what would happen if the dog injured a leg and couldn't walk. She asked for this sling for her birthday and we just gave it a trial run at the house last night. Storm weighs about 35 pounds and is not an easy carry but even positioned in front this sling worked well. My daughter is relieved that she has this solution and happy that it comes in such a small easy-to-carry package.
authors_reviews.author: Diane L Guercio

authors_reviews.title: Bought it for hikes, but needed it in the local park.
authors_reviews.text: I have a 12 yo cattle dog mix who still has the working brain mentality, and forgets her body isn't the same age as her mind. She has a shoulder injury that flares up from time to time, leaving her unable to put weight on one arm. She loves the mountains and hiking, so I bought this for the "in case of emergency" that could happen on a hike. Specifically, I carried it with me yesterday in Breckinridge, and she was fine. She woke up feeling good, we went on our morning walk this today, and she got the zoomies in the park, but had a bed step, and could not finish the walk home. I'm small, so can't carry her the 10 blocks back home, and she also doesn't like be carried (by hand). So I had to call a friend to take us back to my apartment. Lesson learned, I'll now need to bring this with me on local walks as well. I can't say she'll be happy about it, but she'll get over it, and will be thankful I can safely get her home.For reference, she’s 36lbs. The leg holes are snug, but I don’t think she needs to size up.
authors_reviews.author: Kimberly A.

authors_reviews.title: Essential Item
authors_reviews.text: If you love to hike and you want to make sure your pet is taken care of, this is an essential item. It is on the list of essential items for hiking in the white mountains. Sometimes dogs' paws get raw from walking on the granite rock. So, if this happens, I can now take my dog sling out of my back and carry my pup back to safety. It will also work when I take my older dogs on hikes. It is hard to predict when he will get tired, so I will bring this handy sling.
authors_reviews.author: Amazon Customer

authors_reviews.title: Piece of mind
authors_reviews.text: Seems to support and hold both of my puppers well (not at the same time). I hope I will never need this, but I wanted to be prepared should either of my 4-legged hiking buddies ever get hurt on the trail. To be able to safely carry my backpack and one of the girls in case of an emergency gives a me a little piece of mind.
authors_reviews.author: campingirl

authors_reviews.text: The fact that they want $75 for this, which a bit ridiculous for what it is, and then another $40 for the shoulder padding that makes it useable (and should come with it) is totally ridiculous.

other_countries_reviews.title: Not able to use the sling- fit
other_countries_reviews.text: Our medium size staffy cross found this very uncomfortable and we have not been able to use. We measured correctly ,(and have double checked the video) have correct weigh size and followed all the instructions for fitting , we found the sling slipped around the waist and dropped down, and our dog was not secure. we feel it needs some kind of strap which goes around the underneath of the dog and secures at the top of the sling to keep it in place.This is very unfortunate, as we can not use the sling and we really need something as our dog has bad leg. We paid a lot of money for sling and not been able to use once, (only used on a practice round the garden). We would love to be able to use so we can all get out. We should have returned , but did not get round to trying straight away. Any feed back advise to help us to move forward would be appreciated. thanks
